source.title: Where is the Information in a Deep Neural Network?
source.authors: Alessandro Achille; Giovanni Paolini; Stefano Soatto

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses theoretical links between information measures and generalization, and reports measurements of Fisher and Shannon information. Its experiments do not measure test error or the training–test gap, so they do not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The empirical results measure Fisher information, Shannon information and training-path stability, not held-out performance or the training–test gap. The paper also cites prior work on sharp minima and generalization; those cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study develops information-theoretic bounds and measures Fisher information, Shannon information and training-path stability. Its own results do not compare held-out performance or generalization gaps under any V1–V8 intervention. The theoretical connection between Fisher information, stability and generalization does not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness ranking.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors define information through a coding-length versus loss trade-off, connect it to PAC-Bayes generalization bounds, derive an approximate relation involving Fisher information and training stability, and connect weight information to effective representation invariance. Their experiments illustrate information and stability relationships without directly measuring generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops information-theoretic definitions and bounds, then measures Fisher and Shannon information in toy and image-classification settings; it does not reproduce the claim versions’ generalization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes measured Fisher and Shannon information in the toy experiment and measured Fisher information for ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10. The number of CIFAR-10 classes changes measured Fisher information.

fits_no_version.finding: Fisher information rises during learning of increasingly complex classification features, with bumps and subsequent compression phases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fisher information tracks stages of feature learning in the reported toy classification network.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller batches reduce both Fisher and Shannon information in the toy regression experiment; their absolute information estimates differ greatly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD batch size affects Fisher and Shannon information in the reported redundant regression parametrization.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet-18 has lower Fisher trace with smaller batches after 30 epochs and with fewer training classes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured Fisher trace depends on batch size and task class count in these CIFAR-10 experiments.

record.problems: The empirical experiments do not report held-out performance or generalization gaps. Several numerical findings are presented only in figures, without numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The paper itself notes that stability or flatness alone may be insufficient to explain generalization.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy and random-label chance performance.
Width-dependent training interpolation and held-out error beyond interpolation.
Held-out comparisons of convolutional and fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive-optimizer versus SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and recovery through recipe adaptations.
Dropout's effects on held-out error across training-set sizes, dropout strengths and augmentation settings.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance correlated with measured generalization gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and resulting test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 2's All-CNN training-path comparison is omitted from the rows, but it measures stability under replacing one MNIST training example, not a V1–V8 outcome. The warning that flatness alone may be insufficient does not challenge V7's specific correlational claim.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label versus natural-label comparison or held-out accuracy result.
No width sweep or test-error result.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks on held-out error.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers and SGD on held-out performance.
Batch size is varied, but held-out performance and the generalization gap are not measured.
No dropout intervention or held-out error result.
The paper measures Fisher information, but does not test magnitude-aware sharpness or compare a sharpness measure with measured generalization gaps.
No removal of memorized examples or test-accuracy comparison.

rows.subject: simple multi-layer network

rows.measure: Log-determinant of Fisher information during training
rows.value: Figure only; the text says Fisher increases as the network learns increasingly complex features.
rows.note: No test error or training–test gap is reported.
rows.check: Specify a three-layer fully connected network on a 2D binary classification task. Fisher increases during feature learning, with bumps followed by compression phases; this does not measure any version's generalization effect.

rows.subject: toy model with parameter θ
rows.operation_detail: Estimated Shannon information between dataset and parameter, and measured Fisher information, across batch sizes.

conditions.value: B=1, 4, 100; other plotted settings not stated

rows.measure: Shannon information in weights and Fisher information
rows.value: Figure only; text says increasing SGD temperature, for example by reducing batch size, reduces both Fisher and Shannon information. At B=N=100, standard gradient descent maintains the largest information in the weights.
rows.locator: Figure 3 (center); Section 4, “Relation between curvature, Fisher and Shannon Information”
rows.note: The text describes qualitative trends but gives no plotted values. The result does not measure test error or the training–test gap.
rows.check: The task is toy mean regression with N=100 and a redundant scalar parametrization. B=1,4,100 describes the left panel; the center panel has batch-size ticks 1,4,16,64. The text also reports Gaussian information of 4000–5000 nats versus approximately 4 nats of Shannon information. These are information measures, not held-out performance.
